indicators.note: to ginger something up is to liven or stir it, so the following words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A soaking drink described as ginger with more ginger.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'ginger' (to ginger up is to liven) is the anagram signal, not part of the drink; it stirs the following two words into RINGINGWET.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wringing wet is so drenched that water could be squeezed out of it, i.e. thoroughly soaked.

indicators.note: the talk word is placed after the courting and dying pieces

parts.note: to chase a sweetheart is to court or woo
in British slang to rabbit is to talk on and on, to chat

explanation.surface: A rabbit turns up dead after a pursuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is BIRD, the theme, so '18's' reads as 'bird is'. 'Rabbit' as British slang means to chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodchat is a shrike, a small European songbird, so it is an example of the bird theme.

clue.text: Guarantee to protect city area open to attack

indicators.note: one piece protects another by wrapping round it

parts.note: to guarantee against loss is to insure
EC is the postal district of the City of London

explanation.surface: Insurance cover for a city district that is vulnerable to attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Insecure means unprotected or unsafe, so something insecure is exposed to attack.

clue.text: Party welcoming soft successor to Nero

indicators.note: the party takes another piece inside it as a host welcomes a guest

parts.note: a gala is a festive party or celebration
B stands for black, the soft grade of pencil lead

explanation.surface: A party lets in a gentle figure who followed the emperor Nero.
explanation.definitionFit: Galba was the Roman emperor who took the throne after Nero died in AD 68.

clue.text: A salad is no ice cream!

indicators.note: to cream ingredients is to beat them together, so these letters are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: A protest that a dish of salad is not ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cream' looks like part of 'ice cream' but it is the anagram signal working on IS NO ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Salade niçoise, with tuna, olives and egg, is a classic salad from Nice, often called simply a niçoise.

indicators.note: a barrel that is rolling turns over and over, so its letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A wife rolling a barrel along.
explanation.definitionFit: A warbler is any of many small songbirds, so it is an example of the bird theme.

clue.text: Scrap over US Marine uniform that's worn at wedding

indicators.note: over signals the scrap word is turned round

parts.note: an ort is a scrap of leftover food
taken as written
marine means of the sea, so it gives sea
Uniform is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for U

explanation.surface: A fight over the uniform of an American marine at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' turns ORT into TRO. 'Scrap' suggests a fight but means a leftover; 'Marine' looks like a soldier but means the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothing and linen a bride collects for her marriage, much of it worn at and after the wedding.

indicators.note: describes in the sense of drawing a line round, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns, so Y is an unknown

explanation.surface: A doctor describing a mysterious pain.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, to give someone gyp is to cause them pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyp is informal British for pain or trouble, as in 'my back is giving me gyp'.

clue.text: Yours truly comes in to feed, thanks to 23

indicators.note: one piece comes into the middle of the other

parts.note: to graze is to feed on grass
yours truly is the speaker, I

explanation.surface: I arrive to eat and give thanks to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is ITALY, so 'thanks to 23' means thanks in Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Grazie is the Italian word for thank you, so it is Italy's way of giving thanks.

parts.note: a favourite, such as the teacher's favourite, is a pet

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short of its last letter

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: A question about which bank a bird likes best.
explanation.definitionFit: The petrel is a seabird, so it is an example of the bird theme.

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England
L is the usual map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A bird's river and lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ousel is an old name for the blackbird, also used for the dipper and ring ouzel, so it is an example of the bird theme.

clue.text: 18's river entering lake with a roar

indicators.note: the river letter goes inside the lake word

parts.note: Como is a lake in northern Italy
a rant is a loud angry outburst, a roar

explanation.surface: A river flows into a lake with a roar.
explanation.definitionFit: The cormorant is a black fish-eating seabird, so it is an example of the bird theme.

clue.text: 18's only child comes in wanting a tickle?

indicators.note: the child piece comes into the middle of the shuffled letters
wanting means deficient or not right, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: OC is short for only child

explanation.surface: An only child arrives longing to be tickled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' looks like desire but is the anagram signal, making CKATIEL from A TICKLE; OC goes in after the first C.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockatiel is a small crested Australian parrot, so it is an example of the bird theme.

parts.note: to prune a hedge is to snip it

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A bird drinking prune juice.
explanation.definitionFit: The snipe is a long-billed wading bird, so it is an example of the bird theme.

parts.note: at, as in 'at the oars' or 'at arms', means engaged in using
a rifle is a weapon

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone is armed.
explanation.walkthrough: Split differently, the answer reads 'at rifle', someone busy with a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle used as an adverb means a little or somewhat, as in 'a trifle cold'.

parts.note: fair means good or decent, as in fair weather

indicators.note: letters that are unreliable cannot be trusted to stay put, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A bird gets decent but erratic service.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy tern is a small seabird of Australasia, so it is an example of the bird theme.

indicators.note: one might say tells us the word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: the back of something is its rear

explanation.surface: A bird's back, as someone could put it.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless bird of South America, so it is an example of the bird theme.

parts.note: to some believers an ungodly person is a pagan
taken as written
23 is ITALY, whose international vehicle code is I

explanation.surface: A violinist that some people think godless, working in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To some' frames ungodly as an opinion held by some believers.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolò Paganini was a celebrated Italian virtuoso violinist and composer.

clue.text: Always go the wrong way entering junctions

indicators.note: the reversed piece goes inside the junctions word

parts.note: forks in a road are junctions

indicators.note: going the wrong way means the word is read backwards

parts.note: go is a euphemism for urinate, to pee

explanation.surface: A warning about driving the wrong way into road junctions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is a euphemism for relieving oneself; 'the wrong way' gives EEP, which 'entering' places among the junctions.
explanation.definitionFit: For keeps means permanently, so it is an idiom meaning always.

clue.text: Time that's a little bit turned back

indicators.note: turned back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a drib is a small amount, as in dribs and drabs

explanation.surface: Time described as a small piece that has gone backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRD is British slang for a prison sentence, from rhyming slang 'birdlime' for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing bird is British slang for serving time in prison, so it can mean a prison term.

indicators.note: the reversed piece goes into the middle of the bird word

parts.note: 18 is BIRD, and a duck is a bird

indicators.note: turned means the old and news pieces are read backwards

parts.note: N stands for new, so news is NN

explanation.surface: A bird's stale news has been transformed into a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' gives NNO; 'into' places it inside a bird, the second 18 standing for any bird rather than the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The dunnock is the hedge sparrow, a small brown European songbird, so it is an example of the bird theme.

parts.note: a tour is a travelling holiday
A is the first, top choice, as in plan A

explanation.surface: A bird's favourite travel firm.
explanation.definitionFit: The touraco is a colourful African bird, so it is an example of the bird theme.

clue.text: Switched to horse and took up the running

parts.note: taken as written
gee-gee, GG, is a childish word for a horse
to take up the running in a race is to go in front, to lead

explanation.surface: Someone changed to a different horse and went into the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: To toggle is to flick between two settings, so toggled means switched over.

parts.note: a wit is a comic, someone who makes jokes
Kerpow is the noise a punch makes in comic books, suggesting a hit

explanation.surface: In a comic book the word Kerpow implies a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic' looks like a comic book but is the comedian; 'In' alone defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In means fashionable or trendy, as does the informal phrase for being up to date.

parts.note: par is the usual or normal level, as in par for the course
rot is nonsense

explanation.surface: A bird's ordinary nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: The parrot is a brightly coloured talking bird, so it is an example of the bird theme.

clue.text: Even parts of rift valley country

indicators.note: even parts are the letters in the even-numbered positions of the following words

explanation.surface: Bits of a rift valley in some country.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy is a country in southern Europe, so the definition simply names its class.

indicators.note: devouring means one piece swallows the other inside it
merry means tipsy, so the king word is jumbled

parts.note: to thaw is to melt

explanation.surface: A merry king eating a molten dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merry' (tipsy) jumbles the king word into NIGK; 'devouring' has it swallow the hot melt.
explanation.definitionFit: The nighthawk is an American nightjar, so it is an example of the bird theme.

clue.text: Tropical fish netted by pirate trawler

indicators.note: netted by means the fish is caught inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A tropical fish caught in the nets of a pirate trawler.
explanation.definitionFit: The tetra is a small brightly coloured tropical freshwater fish kept in aquariums.

indicators.note: muffling means wrapping round, so the cry encloses the other piece

parts.note: a howl is a loud cry

indicators.note: something that vibrates shakes about, so its letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A cry drowns out a buzzing drone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That vibrates' shakes the drone into ORNED; 'muffling' wraps the cry round it. 'Drone' suggests a buzz, but it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The horned owl has ear tufts like horns, so it is an example of the bird theme.

indicators.note: furious means wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H, so horses is two H's

explanation.surface: A bird furious that its horses have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing' takes the two Hs ('horses', H being heroin) out of WITH THE; 'furious' shuffles the rest, WITTE.
explanation.definitionFit: The twite is a small brown northern finch, so it is an example of the bird theme.

indicators.note: absorbed by means taken inside the other piece

parts.note: TT, the Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle racing on the Isle of Man
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bird engrossed in races.
explanation.definitionFit: The tit is a small songbird such as the blue tit, so it is an example of the bird theme.

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A lakeside scene with fresh flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' looks like it describes the flowers but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Naked ladies is a common name for flowers such as the autumn crocus that bloom without leaves.
